clinician.final_diagnosis: a ruptured renal AML two weeks after COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old female presented to the emergency department with acute-onset left flank pain radiating to the left shoulder, severe left costovertebral angle tenderness, and microhematuria, occurring two weeks after a diagnosed COVID-19 infection. Initial vital signs showed tachycardia (HR 109) with normal blood pressure. Laboratory studies revealed normal coagulation parameters (PT 14s, APTT 35.4s, INR 1.1) and negative pregnancy test. Non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated left peri-renal moderate volume hemorrhage with a 2.5 × 2.3 × 2.1 cm fat-dense lesion in the left kidney, diagnostic of a ruptured renal angiomyolipoma. Twelve hours after admission, interventional radiology performed embolization of the lesion; angiography revealed no aneurysmal dilatation. Post-procedurally, she developed continued hemorrhage with expansion of the retroperitoneal hematoma, hemoglobin nadir of 6.8 g/dl requiring transfusion of 2 units packed red blood cells, and diaphragmatic irritation necessitating supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula. On hospital day 6, she developed recurrent respiratory COVID-19 symptoms with positive PCR testing.

Temporal association with COVID-19 infection (symptom onset two weeks after initial COVID-19 diagnosis, with recurrence on hospital day 6)
